title: Socratic tutor (morning rule)
prompt: You are my tutor for this week's topics: client discovery, architecture docs, scoping, change requests, launch checklists, handover. Do NOT write code for me. Explain concepts, ask one question at a time to check my understanding, and review code I paste. Start by asking what I already know.

title: First-principles explainer
prompt: Explain [CONCEPT] from first principles for a trainee building a forward-deployed client solution. Give: a real-world analogy, the mechanism, a failure scenario, and 3 quiz questions without answers.

title: Quiz me
prompt: Quiz me on [TOPIC] from: client discovery, architecture docs, scoping, change requests, launch checklists, handover. Ask 8 questions of rising difficulty, one at a time, grade each answer and explain mistakes. Finish with weak areas.

title: Debug without giving the answer
when: Stuck during a build (not Saturday: Saturday is no-AI)
prompt: Symptom: [SYMPTOM]. Relevant code/logs (secrets removed): [PASTE]. Do not fix it yet. Give 3 ranked hypotheses, the exact command or log to check each, and what result would confirm or reject it.

title: Code review
prompt: Review this code for scope clarity, measurable success criteria, single points of failure, cost estimate, AI patch safety. List findings by severity with a one-line reason each and a suggested test. Do not rewrite the whole file. Code: [PASTE]

title: Architecture review
prompt: Here is my plan for a forward-deployed client solution: [PLAN]. Review it for single points of failure, missing edge cases, and over-engineering. Give the 3 biggest risks and the smallest change that fixes each.

title: PR review + explain-back drill
when: Before the mentor checks 3 random lines
prompt: Here is my PR diff and description: [DIFF]. First review it like a strict senior engineer. Then pick 3 random changed lines and ask me to explain each; grade my answers honestly. Check my "How I verified this" section is real.

title: Weekly learning plan
prompt: I'm starting a week on: client discovery, architecture docs, scoping, change requests, launch checklists, handover. I have mornings for hand-coding and afternoons to build with AI. Make a day-by-day plan with active-recall tasks, one thing to build by hand per morning, and one thing to verify per afternoon.

title: Mock interview
prompt: Act as an interviewer for a full-stack AI developer role. Ask me 10 questions on: client discovery, architecture docs, scoping, change requests, launch checklists, handover. Mix concept, debugging and design. One at a time, give feedback, then a score and a list of topics to revisit.
